info.name: music-playback-service (E3-SS-02)
info.description: Manual/scripted verification for POST /v1/playback/events and :batch, added by E3-SS-02. By default (mintOwnToken=true) it mints its own HS256 tokens via a collection-level pre-request script (CryptoJS), so it never needs music-identity-gatekeeper running — jwtSecret just has to match whatever JWT_SECRET the target playback-service instance was started with. Set mintOwnToken=false to instead run both services locally (matching JWT_SECRET in each's .env) and use a REAL token from music-identity-gatekeeper's own Postman collection's Login request, or POST {{migUrl}}/auth/login by hand — paste it into the accessToken variable yourself and this collection leaves it alone. Full narrative test plan: Docs/tickets/E3-SS-02/TEST_PLAN.md.

exec: // Mints two fresh HS256 access tokens before every request in this
// jwtSecret MUST equal the running music-playback-service's JWT_SECRET
// (and, in a real deployment, music-identity-gatekeeper's — they must
// share one secret since playback only verifies, never issues, tokens).
// This collection deliberately does NOT depend on identity-gatekeeper
// being up: the algorithm below (base64url header/payload + HMAC-SHA256)
// is the exact same one music-identity-gatekeeper/internal/token uses,
// independently re-verified against a live playback-service instance
// using Node's built-in crypto module before this collection was written.
const payload = { user_id: userId, tier: 'free', exp: now + expiresInSeconds, iat: now };
// Set collection variable mintOwnToken to "false" to use a REAL token
// from a running music-identity-gatekeeper instead (e.g. via its own
// Postman collection's "2. Login" request, or POST {{migUrl}}/auth/login
// by hand) — paste it into the accessToken variable yourself and this
// script will leave it alone. Folder 1 ("Auth - Negative")'s wrong-secret
// and expired-token requests always self-mint regardless of this flag,
// since those scenarios are meaningless against a real valid token.
// Folder 4 ("Identity & Per-User Scoping") needs a second real user's
// token in accessTokenB to run against a real identity-gatekeeper — not
// automated here; register a second user by hand if you want that folder
// to use real tokens too, or just leave mintOwnToken=true for it.

variable.description: music-identity-gatekeeper base URL — only used as a reference/reminder for the real-token workflow (mintOwnToken=false); this collection never calls it itself.

"true" (default): self-mint both HS256 tokens every request, no identity-gatekeeper needed. "false": leave accessToken/accessTokenB alone so you can paste in a real token from identity-gatekeeper's login flow.

MUST match the target playback-service instance's JWT_SECRET exactly (and, if mintOwnToken=false, music-identity-gatekeeper's too), or every request 401s with INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN. Defaults to this repo's own local-dev placeholder value from both services' .env files.
Auto-generated on collection run start if empty; reused across requests so events/batches reference a consistent song.

item.name: 14a. context At True Boundary (4095 Wire Bytes -> 4096 Stored) -> Accepted

exec: // Computes a single-key JSON object whose OWN text is exactly `target`
// bytes on the wire, measured at runtime rather than assumed.
// A compact (no-whitespace) single-key object has exactly one ':' —
// Postgres's jsonb type adds a space after it on storage, so a wire
// payload of N bytes here is stored as N+1 bytes. 4095 wire bytes is
// therefore the TRUE boundary that lands at exactly the DB's 4096-byte
// stored cap, not 4096 wire bytes as a naive reading of the spec ("4 KiB")
// would suggest. See Docs/common/DECISIONS_AND_GOTCHAS.md for the full story
// — this collection is what caught the bug in the first place.
